topics.label: Lecture framing and introduction to cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture's learning outcomes and its use of cancer hallmarks to connect mutations with changes in tumour behaviour.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation alters cancer cell populations and tissue organisation in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of the p53–Bax pathway or increased BCL2 activity prevents cancer cells from undergoing apoptosis.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome telomere-dependent limits on replication by restoring telomerase expression.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of intrinsic growth-control safeguards by explaining p53-dependent stress responses and reviewing how mutations undermine normal growth control.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the genetic and epigenetic changes that drive it.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in tumour development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why tumour growth requires an angiogenic switch and how that switch emerges during tumour development.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells reach and establish distant tumours, highlighting the barriers to successful metastasis and the difficulty of identifying a distinct metastatic genetic signature.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's learning goals, emphasises convergence on shared cancer hallmarks and offers further reading before the farewell.
